facts.fact_text: At approximately 6 a.m. on 1 May 2008, members of the Confederation of Progressive Trade Unions of Turkey (DİSK) and the Confederation of Public Employees' Trade Unions (KESK) began gathering in front of the DİSK headquarters located in the district of Şişli for Labour Day celebrations.

The members of the group refused to disperse, arguing that they were merely waiting in front of the DİSK headquarters, which was a pedestrian area, and that they were not violating the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) in any way.
At around 6.30 a.m. on 1 May 2008, the police asked the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli to disperse.
The police warned the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli that they were acting in violation of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911).
The police proceeded to disperse the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli by spraying them with pressurised water, paint and tear gas, both inside and outside the DİSK building.
Similar police interventions occurred over the next couple of hours after 6.30 a.m. on 1 May 2008 with increasing intensity.
Some of the demonstrators were injured as a result of the use of force by the police on 1 May 2008 in the district of Şişli.
While injured demonstrators were trying to reach the nearby Şişli Etfal Hospital for medical care, they were chased by the police.
While injured demonstrators were trying to reach Şişli Etfal Hospital for medical care, they were subjected to gas attacks even within the hospital premises.
Article 34 of the Turkish Constitution provides that everyone has the right to hold unarmed and peaceful meetings and demonstration marches without prior permission.

Article 34 of the Turkish Constitution provides that the formalities, conditions, and procedures governing the exercise of the right to hold meetings and demonstration marches shall be prescribed by law.
Section 22 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) prohibits demonstrations and processions on public streets, in parks, places of worship and buildings in which public services are based.

Section 22 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that demonstrations organised in public squares have to comply with security instructions and not disrupt individuals' movements or public transport.

Section 24 of the Assemblies and Marches Act (Law no. 2911) provides that demonstrations and processions which do not comply with the provisions of that law will be dispersed by force on the order of the governor's office and after the demonstrators are warned.

The Minister of the Interior issued a press statement declaring that the authorities were in possession of intelligence reports which precluded them from authorising any demonstration in Taksim Square, for security reasons.

The Government's spokesman issued a press statement declaring that the authorities were in possession of intelligence reports which precluded them from authorising any demonstration in Taksim Square, for security reasons.

The Istanbul Governor's office issued a press statement declaring that the authorities were in possession of intelligence reports which precluded them from authorising any demonstration in Taksim Square, for security reasons.
The authorities held that any demonstration held in Taksim Square on 1 May 2008 would be unlawful and unconstitutional on account of possible provocations and disruption of traffic and public order.
The authorities stated that they were going to block the roads leading to Taksim Square on 1 May 2008 as a security measure.
The authorities stated that they were going to deploy extra police on 1 May 2008 as a security measure.
The police proceeded to disperse the group gathered in front of the DİSK headquarters in Şişli by spraying them with pressurised water, paint and tear gas, both inside and outside the DİSK building.
Similar police interventions occurred over the next couple of hours after 6.30 a.m. on 1 May 2008 with increasing intensity.
Some of the demonstrators were injured as a result of the use of force by the police on 1 May 2008 in the district of Şişli.
While injured demonstrators were trying to reach the nearby Şişli Etfal Hospital for medical care, they were chased by the police.
While injured demonstrators were trying to reach Şişli Etfal Hospital for medical care, they were subjected to gas attacks even within the hospital premises.

The Chief of Şişli Etfal Hospital stated that police officers had entered the Şişli Etfal Hospital premises in pursuit of the demonstrators and used a gas bomb in the hospital's garden to neutralise the demonstrators.

The Chief of Şişli Etfal Hospital stated that one of the police officers had mistakenly sat on a gas bomb and exploded it in the police car parked at the entrance of the Emergency Service of Şişli Etfal Hospital.

The Chief of Şişli Etfal Hospital stated that as a result of the gas bomb explosion in the police car, staff working in the Emergency Service of Şişli Etfal Hospital as well as some of the patients had been affected.
The Chief of Şişli Etfal Hospital stated that the gas bomb was not deliberately thrown in the hospital building.
On 30 April 2008 the first applicant lodged a complaint against the Governor of Istanbul with the Istanbul public prosecutor.
The first applicant accused the Governor of Istanbul of denying the trade unions their right to assembly in a discriminatory manner.

The first applicant complained that there was no justification for denying trade unions access to Taksim Square on Labour Day, when the same location was available for other large-scale demonstrations and celebrations.
The complaint lodged by the first applicant against the Governor of Istanbul was assigned investigation number 2008/20905.

On an unspecified date, the Istanbul public prosecutor issued a decision of lack of jurisdiction in connection with the complaint lodged against the Istanbul Governor and the Head of Istanbul Security Directorate.
The case file concerning the complaint against the Istanbul Governor and the Head of Istanbul Security Directorate was transferred to the Public Prosecutor's Office at the Court of Cassation.

Pursuant to the terms of Law no. 4483, the public prosecutor at the Court of Cassation sought authorisation from the Minister of the Interior to prosecute the Istanbul Governor and the Head of Istanbul Security Directorate.
On an unspecified date, the Minister of the Interior refused to authorise the prosecution of the Istanbul Governor and the Head of Istanbul Security Directorate.
On 8 April 2009 the public prosecutor at the Court of Cassation decided not to proceed with the case against the Istanbul Governor and the Head of Istanbul Security Directorate.
The decision of 8 April 2009 not to proceed with the case was notified to the applicants' lawyer on 16 April 2009.
The applicants' appeal lodged against the decision of 8 April 2009 not to proceed with the case was dismissed by the Supreme Administrative Court.
The Supreme Administrative Court held that pursuant to domestic legislation, no appeal was possible against the decision of 8 April 2009 not to proceed with the case.

On 1 February 2009 the Istanbul public prosecutor delivered a decision of non-prosecution regarding the complaint lodged against the Prime Minister, the Minister of the Interior, and the Minister of Justice.

The Istanbul public prosecutor held that pursuant to the Turkish Constitution, the Prime Minister, the Minister of the Interior, and the Minister of Justice could not be held liable for their actions in the course of their duties.
The decision of non-prosecution dated 1 February 2009 was served on the applicants' lawyer on 24 February 2009.
The applicants' appeal against the decision of non-prosecution dated 1 February 2009 was rejected on 22 May 2009 by the Sincan Assize Court.
The Sincan Assize Court held that no objection could be lodged against the decision of the Istanbul public prosecutor dated 1 February 2009.
No prosecution was initiated against the applicants in relation to the events of 1 May 2008.
